\section*{Growth model}
The quarterly growth rate follows from the ratio of consecutive revenues:
\[
  g_t = \frac{R_t - R_{t-1}}{R_{t-1}}, \qquad
  \bar{g} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{t=1}^{n} g_t, \qquad
  \sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{t=1}^{n} \left(g_t - \bar{g}\right)^2 .
\]
Compounded over a year the rate is
\[
  G = \prod_{t=1}^{4} \left(1 + g_t\right) - 1 = \exp\!\Big(\sum_{t=1}^{4} \ln(1+g_t)\Big) - 1 .
\]
\newpage
\section*{Transition matrix}
Customers move between plans each quarter with these probabilities:
\[
  P = \begin{pmatrix} 0.82 & 0.15 & 0.03 \\ 0.10 & 0.80 & 0.10 \\ 0.02 & 0.18 & 0.80 \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad \pi P = \pi .
\]
